scenes.title: Physical Settlement vs. Cash ISDA Credit Auctions

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Physical Settlement: protection buyer delivers eligible senior unsecured bonds in exchange for par value 100%, exploiting cheapest-to-deliver optionality ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Compare Cash Settlement: ISDA credit auction establishes market recovery value $Z\%$, and protection seller pays $100\% - Z\%$ in cash ([fact-03]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Deconstructing Hazard Rates & CDS Leg Pricing Equivalence

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Hazard Rate Formula: $\lambda = s / (1 - R)$ linking yield spread $s$ to default intensity given recovery rate $R$ ([fact-04]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Break down Pricing Equivalence: $PV(	ext{Premium Leg}) = PV(	ext{Protection Leg})$ equating expected periodic spread inflows to contingent default losses ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Examine Senior Tranches: Mezzanine (3-7%), Senior (7-10%), and Super Senior Tranche absorbing remaining losses from 10% to 100% ([fact-09]).

scenes.title: Gaussian Copula Assumptions vs. Real-World Tail Dependence

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Gaussian Copula Simplicity: reducing joint default distributions to a single correlation parameter for Wall Street tranche pricing ([fact-10]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Balance Tail Dependence Reality: assuming zero tail dependence masked catastrophic correlation risk during 2007-2008 systemic market panics ([fact-10]).

scenes.title: CDS Premium Leg Cashflows vs. Contingent Protection Payoffs

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot Premium Leg Inflows: periodic spread payments ($s \cdot q_i \cdot e^{-rt_i}$) received until default or maturity ([fact-05]).
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Plot Protection Payoff Leg: contingent recovery loss $(1 - R) \cdot p_i \cdot e^{-rt_i^*}$ paid upon reference entity default ([fact-05]).

summarySteps: 1. Credit Default Swap (CDS) ([fact-01]): Bilateral financial contract providing periodic premium protection against reference entity default.
2. ISDA Credit Events ([fact-02]): Legal criteria including bankruptcy, failure to pay, and debt restructuring.
3. Settlement Options ([fact-03]): Physical delivery with cheapest-to-deliver optionality versus cash settlement via ISDA credit auctions.
4. Hazard Rate Formula ([fact-04]): $\lambda = s / (1 - R)$ estimating default intensity from yield spreads and recovery rates.
5. Fair Spread Pricing ([fact-05]): Equating present value of premium payment leg to contingent protection payoff leg.
6. Credit Indices ([fact-08]): Standardized 125-name portfolios (CDX and iTraxx) serving as institutional macro credit benchmarks.
7. Synthetic CDO Tranches ([fact-09]): Priority loss waterfalls slicing portfolio risk from Equity (0-3%) to Super Senior (10-100%).
8. Gaussian Copula & Regulation ([fact-10], [fact-11]): Zero tail dependence caused 2007-2008 copula failure, prompting post-2008 CCP clearing mandates.
bottomTakeaway: Credit derivatives unbundle default risk into tradable instruments like Credit Default Swaps and Synthetic CDOs, anchored by hazard rate pricing while requiring robust central clearing and awareness of copula tail-risk limitations ([fact-01], [fact-04], [fact-09], [fact-10], [fact-11]).
